I added the comment line to `scripts/check.sh` directly above where `CHECK_LIMIT_KB` is read. The syntax check passes and nothing is committed.

**PRECEDENT.md:** `scripts/PRECEDENT.md` exists. The repo root has no PRECEDENT.md; the other four are under `src/` and don't cover scripts. The one decision for check.sh is §check-fails-open:
> - Decision: `set -uo pipefail` without `-e`. Every internal error still ends in `exit 0`; the script only warns.
> - Forbidden: `set -e` or `set -o errexit`, and any exit status other than 0.

It says nothing about comments, header style, `CHECK_LIMIT_KB` or its default, so it doesn't conflict with this task. A comment doesn't change `set` or the exit status, so the decision still holds. Since this isn't a new decision, I didn't add anything to PRECEDENT.md.

**Where the default comes from:** `scripts/check.sh:5` (line 6 after the edit), `limit_kb=${CHECK_LIMIT_KB:-512}`. That is the only place in the repo that mentions `CHECK_LIMIT_KB`, so the default is clearly 512 KB.

**`git diff`:**
```
diff --git a/scripts/check.sh b/scripts/check.sh
index ca11304..59b3221 100755
--- a/scripts/check.sh

@@ -2,6 +2,7 @@
 # Advisory pre-commit check: warns about large staged files.
 set -uo pipefail
 
+# CHECK_LIMIT_KB: size threshold in KB above which a staged file is reported (default 512).
 limit_kb=${CHECK_LIMIT_KB:-512}
 big=$(git diff --cached --name-only 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
   [ -f "$f" ] || continue
```
